c.tagline: Java's cool-highland city of Art Deco, factory outlets, and volcano views.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird is the trusted metered taxi brand; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front pricing and metered motorbike rides.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service.

hood_landmark.Dago (Ir. H. Djuanda): Jalan Ir. H. Djuanda Dago, Bandung

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in Pasar Baru and on crowded angkot minibuses, and keep phones out of snatching reach in traffic.

hood_desc: The atmospheric heart of old Bandung: a pedestrian-friendly street of restored 1920s Art Deco facades, cafes, galleries and the city's colonial landmarks; best for first-timers who want history within walking distance.

The leafy uphill spine of Jalan Ir. H. Djuanda, lined with cafes, restaurants, factory outlets and boutique hotels as it climbs toward cooler air; suits travelers who want dining and shopping with a view.
Bandung's famous 'jeans street' and mall district, packed with denim shops, factory outlets and the Cihampelas Walk (Ciwalk) mall; best for shoppers and bargain-hunters.
The civic core around Alun-Alun square and the Grand Mosque, close to Pasar Baru market and the intercity stations; a central, well-connected base in the middle of everything.
The cooler leafy uplands toward Setiabudi, Ciumbuleuit and Lembang, with resort hotels, family parks and highland calm a short drive from the crowded center; suits those wanting quiet and fresh air.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: Trans Metro Bandung buses and angkot run roughly 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM; angkot taper off in the evening, when Gojek/Grab fill the gap.
transit.note: Bandung has no metro or tram; getting around means the Trans Metro Bandung / Trans Metro Pasundan bus corridors, the ubiquitous angkot (colored share-minivans), the KA Commuter Bandung Raya line linking Padalarang-Bandung-Cicalengka, plus Gojek/Grab motorbikes and cars.
transit.pay: Angkot and city buses are paid in cash to the driver (a few thousand rupiah); ride-hailing apps and QRIS e-wallets are widely used for door-to-door trips. There is no unified transit card.

sys.n: Trans Metro Bandung / Trans Metro Pasundan (BRT)

air: Kertajati International Airport (KJT), ~68 km east, handles most jet services
bus: Trans Metro Bandung / Trans Metro Pasundan
Intercity buses from Leuwipanjang & Cicaheum terminals to Jakarta, Bogor and across Java

car.idp: Recommended (International Driving Permit required alongside home license)

train: Bandung Station intercity trains to Jakarta, Yogyakarta and Surabaya
Whoosh high-speed rail (Jakarta-Bandung) at Padalarang/Tegalluar stations

transit.m: Damri airport bus / angkot to city center (~20-30 min)
Airport taxi to central Bandung (15-25 min)
Kertajati Airport (KJT) ~68 km east handles most jet flights; Damri bus connects it to Bandung (~2.5-3 hrs)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a service charge is often included at mid-range restaurants, and rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Batagor
food.desc: Bandung's signature snack: fried fish-paste dumplings and tofu drenched in thick peanut sauce with lime, kecap and chilli.

places.name: Batagor Kingsley
places.note: Trading since the 1980s and still the benchmark; pricier than street batagor but famously good peanut sauce.

places.name: Batagor Riri
places.note: Kingsley's closest rival, run on a family recipe for decades and always busy at lunch.

places.name: Alun-Alun and Braga street carts
places.note: Cheap carts around the main square and Jalan Braga serve batagor from mid-afternoon.

food.name: Siomay Bandung
food.desc: Steamed fish and tofu dumplings with cabbage roll, potato and boiled egg, smothered in peanut sauce - the steamed cousin of batagor.

places.name: Batagor Kingsley
places.note: Serves the steamed siomay version alongside the fried one; order both to compare.

places.name: Batagor Riri
places.note: Generous plates of siomay with the same house peanut sauce.

places.name: Pasar Cihapit food stalls
places.note: Old neighbourhood market where locals eat siomay and other jajanan in the morning.

food.name: Mie kocok
food.desc: Flat yellow noodles in a rich beef-bone broth with tender kikil (cow tendon), beansprouts, lime and fried shallots.

places.name: Mie Kocok Mang Dadeng
places.note: The name locals give first; thick broth and soft kikil, often sold out before evening.

places.name: Mie Kocok Persib
places.note: Long-running mie kocok stall named after the city's football club, a classic cheap breakfast.

places.name: Pasar Cihapit warungs
places.note: Market noodle stalls doing morning bowls at a fraction of restaurant prices.

food.name: Nasi timbel & Sundanese lalapan
food.desc: Rice steamed in banana leaf with fried chicken or gurame fish, tofu, tempeh, raw vegetables and fiery sambal terasi.

places.name: Nasi Bancakan
places.note: Retro Sundanese canteen where you pick dishes from clay pots; hugely popular with locals.

places.name: Warung Nasi Ampera
places.note: Bandung's best-known Sundanese chain, open long hours and easy to order by pointing.

places.name: Sindang Reret
places.note: Established Sundanese restaurant known for grilled fish and traditional set meals.

food.name: Surabi
food.desc: Small rice-flour pancakes cooked in clay pans over charcoal - traditional oncom or kinca palm syrup, or modern cheese and chocolate.

places.name: Surabi Cihapit
places.note: Long-standing surabi spot doing both traditional and modern toppings.

places.name: Surabi Enhaii
places.note: Bandung institution near the tourism school, busy from late afternoon into the night.

places.name: Pasar Cihapit morning stalls
places.note: Charcoal-fired surabi sold at the market before 9am, the way locals eat it.

food.name: Peuyeum & cireng
food.desc: Peuyeum is fermented cassava, sweet and faintly boozy in taste, hung in bunches; cireng are chewy fried tapioca cakes with spicy dip.

places.name: Jalan Cihampelas peuyeum sellers
places.note: Bunches of peuyeum hang from roadside stalls along the shopping street.

places.name: Pasar Baru Trade Centre
places.note: Market floors selling peuyeum, cireng and other Sundanese snacks to take away.

places.name: Kartika Sari
places.note: The classic Bandung oleh-oleh shop for packaged local snacks and cakes.

food.name: Bandrek & bajigur
food.desc: Hot Sundanese drinks: bandrek is ginger, palm sugar and spice; bajigur adds coconut milk and coffee. Made for cool highland evenings.

places.name: Lembang roadside warungs
places.note: Stalls on the mountain road serve bandrek with grilled corn on cold nights.

places.name: Kampung Daun
places.note: Garden restaurant in a valley of thatched huts, classic spot for a hot bandrek.

places.name: Dago Pakar viewpoint stalls
places.note: Simple warungs above the city selling bandrek and bajigur with a night view.

food.name: Es cendol & es goyobod
food.desc: Iced sweets you drink: green rice-flour worms or diced hunkwe jelly in coconut milk and palm sugar, with shaved ice and avocado.

places.name: Cendol Elizabeth
places.note: Bandung's most famous cendol, sold from a simple counter; expect a queue.

places.name: Es Goyobod Kliningan
places.note: Long-running goyobod stall, the local variant with hunkwe cubes and avocado.

places.name: Pasar Cihapit stalls
places.note: Cheap cendol and es campur made fresh in the market each morning.

landmarks: Gedung Sate
Bandung's iconic 1920 Art Deco-meets-Indies government building, named for the satay-skewer ornament crowning its central tower.
Museum of the Asian-African Conference (Gedung Merdeka)
The historic hall where Sukarno, Nehru, and Zhou Enlai launched the Non-Aligned movement at the landmark 1955 Bandung Conference.
Braga Street
The romantic colonial-era boulevard of Art Deco facades, cafés, and galleries that earned Bandung its 'Paris of Java' nickname.
Saung Angklung Udjo
A joyous cultural village where daily performances of bamboo angklung orchestras, wayang puppets, and Sundanese dance end with everyone playing along.
Tebing Keraton
A clifftop lookout above the Dago forest where dawn crowds watch mist drift through the Ciharegem valley's pine canopy.
Villa Isola
A streamline-moderne 1933 masterpiece set in terraced gardens, considered one of Southeast Asia's finest Art Deco buildings.
Lembang Floating Market
A family-friendly lakeside bazaar in the cool Lembang highlands, where vendors sell Sundanese snacks from wooden boats.
Ciater Hot Springs (Sari Ater)
Steaming volcanic pools cascading through tea plantations below Tangkuban Perahu, perfect for a therapeutic soak in the mountain air.
Taman Hutan Raya Ir. H. Djuanda
A forested conservation park in the hills above Bandung with walking trails, waterfalls, and Dutch-era bunkers carved into a winding river valley.
Trans Studio Bandung
Indonesia's largest indoor theme park, with three themed zones of rides, live shows and attractions built into a sprawling shopping mall complex.

train.note: No international trains. The Whoosh high-speed line has transformed the Jakarta run - about 45 minutes from Halim to Tegalluar/Padalarang, versus three hours on the road. Conventional KAI trains from Bandung station also run the classic scenic route to Jakarta through the Puncak hills, and east to Yogyakarta and Surabaya. Book Whoosh on ticket.kcic.co.id and KAI services on the KAI Access app.

bus.note: No international coaches. Terminal Leuwipanjang serves the west and Cicaheum the east, with frequent buses to Jakarta and Bogor; the door-to-door travel minibuses (Cititrans, DayTrans, Baraya) that run from small city offices are more popular than the big terminals for the Jakarta route. Book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/) or the operators' own apps.

ferry.note: Bandung sits in a highland basin ringed by volcanoes, well inland, so there are no ferries. The nearest ports are on the north coast at Jakarta and Cirebon.

half.name: Tangkuban Perahu
half.blurb: Drive-up volcanic crater ~30 km north with steaming fumaroles and rim views over the Lembang highlands.

half.name: Ciwidey & Kawah Putih
half.blurb: Surreal turquoise volcanic crater lake ~50 km south, ringed by tea plantations and Situ Patenggang lake.

full.name: Garut
full.blurb: Highland town famed for Cipanas hot springs, Kamojang crater and dodol sweets, ~2.5 hrs southeast.
